definitions.explanation: A unit of length equal to one hundredth of a meter. The everyday unit of length in Japan for small-to-medium measurements such as clothing sizes, furniture, and body measurements. Often shortened to センチ in casual speech.

examples.japanese: ⟦{身長|しんちょう}→身長：03263_shinchou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧175センチメートルです。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦テーブル→テーブル：04488_teeburu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{幅|はば}→幅：03565_haba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧90センチメートル⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦{雪|ゆき}→雪：00584_yuki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一晩|ひとばん}→一晩：08887_hitoban⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧30センチメートル⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{積|つ}もった→積もる：01964_tsumoru⟧。
examples.english: About 30 centimeters of snow piled up in a single night.

notes:
Japan uses the metric system, and センチメートル (often written cm) is the standard unit for everyday length measurements. In casual speech and writing, the shortened form ⟦センチ→センチ：01372_senchi⟧ is far more common than the full form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{何|なん}→何〜：03100_nan⟧センチメートル: how many centimeters
- センチメートル⟦{単位|たんい}→単位：03412_tani⟧: in units of centimeters
- ～センチメートル⟦{伸|の}びる→伸びる：01974_nobiru⟧: to grow by ~ centimeters
- ～センチメートル⟦{離|はな}れる→離れる：02397_hanareru⟧: to be ~ centimeters apart

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦センチ→センチ：01372_senchi⟧: centimeter — the casual shortened form, used far more often in daily conversation
- ⟦ミリメートル→ミリメートル：23178_mirimeetoru⟧: millimeter — one tenth of a centimeter; used for finer measurements
- ⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧: meter — one hundred centimeters; used for longer distances
- ⟦{尺|しゃく}→尺：26043_shaku⟧: shaku — traditional Japanese unit (~30.3 cm), now rarely used outside traditional crafts

USAGE:
When writing, the abbreviation cm is extremely common. In speech, ⟦センチ→センチ：01372_senchi⟧ is used almost exclusively for body and object measurements (e.g., ⟦{身長|しんちょう}→身長：03263_shinchou⟧170⟦センチ→センチ：01372_senchi⟧). The full form センチメートル appears mainly in technical, educational, or formal contexts.
